claims_disputed.claim: On 200 SWE-bench Verified tasks, delivering CodeNib candidates and retiring them after the first read (compact) resolves 79 vs 66 for on-demand exploration and 56 for Aider's repo map.
claims_disputed.reason: Several problems compound. It is one run per cell, and repeats flipped outcomes on 2/10 (compact) and 4/10 (on-demand) tasks. The worst-case p over unknown fills is 0.0502, above the predeclared 0.05, and the complete-pair estimate was written post hoc (§10.2). The repository-clustered interval [-3.92, +17.42] spans zero, and the effect is carried by Django and xarray. The 79-vs-56 Aider comparison mixes two factors, candidate source and retention, and the eager-vs-Aider secondary contrast is not reported as surviving Holm. Finally, CodeNib's 149 s per-task view build sits outside the USD 1 budget, while On-demand pays nothing (§9.9).

pattern_stance_changes.reason: No budget or cap is tested as a harness intervention. The cap is a fixed condition that constrains outcomes, and raising it to USD 2 lifts both arms (50 vs 46). The evidence is about context size under a cap, not about caps being beneficial.
The usefulness of traces is asserted, not tested. The fidelity findings come from offline comparisons against rebuilds and live servers, not from an observability intervention.

In Q6, localization differences span zero (File Recall@5 +8.70 [-12.41, +29.50]), and an earlier ten-task study showed a 17.5-point deficit. The completion gain is attributed to response length rather than graph structure (§9.8). Static references match live servers only 64% of the time, and symbol-graph repair matches a rebuild on 13/24 changes.

missed_issues: The Q7 harness was built and tuned on 50 Verified tasks, which were excluded from the 200. However, Q6 was rerun on the same cohort after two of the authors' own interface defects were found, so the 'agents we did not write' framing overstates how independent the evaluation is (§10.2).

The repair cost comparison is not equal-resource. The USD 1 stop rule covers only agent execution, while CodeNib's per-task view construction (mean 149.21 s including model loading) is excluded and On-demand has none (§9.9). This is missing_cost_reporting at the headline level.

Codex assisted with protocol design, analysis code and failure diagnosis for the held-out and repair studies (§9.1), and the residual navigation case study is AI-assisted rather than human-annotated. This adds unvalidated-tooling risk on top of the opus-generated, opus-judged Q5 workload.

Relevance 4 is generous. No study includes Java or jdtls, and no study includes cross-repository queries (every view is per repo and commit). The applicability text's '20-87%' token-cut figure merges Q6's 20% with Q5's synthetic-workload figures.
Reproducibility 2 is generous given that no code or data URL appears anywhere in the text. That is closer to 1.
note: A carefully reported, academically independent system paper whose index-fidelity findings (incremental repair must be checked against a rebuild) are its most robust contribution. The headline end-to-end repair and localization gains are fragile: one model, one run, and significance at the threshold.
